knowledge_point.title: Expressing Flux Over a Surface as a Repeated Integral

question.:question/problem:
Consider the vector field $\mathbf F(x,y,z)=⟨y - z,\,- 2 y + z,\,- xy⟩$ and the surface $S$ defined by $z=x - y$ for $1\le x\le 5$ and $-2\le y\le 5$. Orient $S$ so that its normal has a positive $\mathbf k$-component.

Using the parametrization $x=u$ and $y=v$, the flux through $S$ can be expressed as

$$
\iint_S\mathbf F\cdot\mathrm d\mathbf S={\int }_{1}^{5}{\int }_{-2}^{5}\boxed{\phantom{AAAAAAA}}\,\text{d}v\,\text{d}u.
$$

What is the missing expression?
question.:question/worked-solution:
The parametrization and its parameter domain are

$$
\mathbf r(u,v)=⟨u,\,v,\,u - v⟩
$$



$$
D=\{(u,v):1\le u\le 5,\ -2\le v\le 5\}.
$$

Differentiate and compute the natural vector area element:

$$
\begin{aligned}\mathbf r_u&=⟨1,\,0,\,1⟩ \\ \mathbf r_v&=⟨0,\,1,\,-1⟩ \\ \mathbf r_u\times\mathbf r_v&=\begin{vmatrix}\mathbf i & \mathbf j & \mathbf k \\ 1 & 0 & 1 \\ 0 & 1 & -1\end{vmatrix} \\ &=⟨-1,\,1,\,1⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

The cross product already has the requested orientation, so

$$
\mathbf N=\mathbf r_u\times\mathbf r_v=⟨-1,\,1,\,1⟩.
$$

Write $\mathbf F=\langle P,Q,R\rangle$. Substitute all three coordinates into each component:

$$
\begin{aligned}P(\mathbf r(u,v))&=(v) - (u - v) \\ &=- u + 2 v.\end{aligned}
$$



$$
\begin{aligned}Q(\mathbf r(u,v))&=- 2 (v) + (u - v) \\ &=u - 3 v.\end{aligned}
$$



$$
\begin{aligned}R(\mathbf r(u,v))&=- (u)(v) \\ &=- uv.\end{aligned}
$$

Form the oriented dot product and collect like terms:

$$
I(u,v)=\mathbf F(\mathbf r(u,v))\cdot\mathbf N.
$$

Its three contributions are

$$
\begin{aligned}T_1&=(- u + 2 v)(-1) \\ &=u - 2 v.\end{aligned}
$$



$$
\begin{aligned}T_2&=(u - 3 v)(1) \\ &=u - 3 v.\end{aligned}
$$



$$
\begin{aligned}T_3&=(- uv)(1) \\ &=- uv.\end{aligned}
$$

Adding them gives the missing integrand:

$$
\begin{aligned}I(u,v)&=T_1+T_2+T_3 \\ &=- uv + 2 u - 5 v.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore,

$$
\iint_S\mathbf F\cdot\mathrm d\mathbf S={\int }_{1}^{5}{\int }_{-2}^{5}I(u,v)\,\text{d}v\,\text{d}u.
$$

The missing expression is $- uv + 2 u - 5 v$.

knowledge_point.title: Expressing Flux Over a Surface as a Repeated Integral

question.:question/problem:
Consider the vector field $\mathbf F(x,y,z)=⟨x + z,\,2 z,\,y + z⟩$ and the surface $S$ defined by $z=- x - y$ for $1\le x\le 3$ and $-2\le y\le 4$. Orient $S$ so that its normal has a positive $\mathbf k$-component.

Using the parametrization $x=u$ and $y=v$, the flux through $S$ can be expressed as

$$
\iint_S\mathbf F\cdot\mathrm d\mathbf S={\int }_{1}^{3}{\int }_{-2}^{4}\boxed{\phantom{AAAAAAA}}\,\text{d}v\,\text{d}u.
$$

What is the missing expression?
question.:question/worked-solution:
The parametrization and its parameter domain are

$$
\mathbf r(u,v)=⟨u,\,v,\,- u - v⟩
$$



$$
D=\{(u,v):1\le u\le 3,\ -2\le v\le 4\}.
$$

Differentiate and compute the natural vector area element:

$$
\begin{aligned}\mathbf r_u&=⟨1,\,0,\,-1⟩ \\ \mathbf r_v&=⟨0,\,1,\,-1⟩ \\ \mathbf r_u\times\mathbf r_v&=\begin{vmatrix}\mathbf i & \mathbf j & \mathbf k \\ 1 & 0 & -1 \\ 0 & 1 & -1\end{vmatrix} \\ &=⟨1,\,1,\,1⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

The cross product already has the requested orientation, so

$$
\mathbf N=\mathbf r_u\times\mathbf r_v=⟨1,\,1,\,1⟩.
$$

Write $\mathbf F=\langle P,Q,R\rangle$. Substitute all three coordinates into each component:

$$
\begin{aligned}P(\mathbf r(u,v))&=(u) + (- u - v) \\ &=- v.\end{aligned}
$$



$$
\begin{aligned}Q(\mathbf r(u,v))&=2 (- u - v) \\ &=- 2 u - 2 v.\end{aligned}
$$



$$
\begin{aligned}R(\mathbf r(u,v))&=(v) + (- u - v) \\ &=- u.\end{aligned}
$$

Form the oriented dot product and collect like terms:

$$
I(u,v)=\mathbf F(\mathbf r(u,v))\cdot\mathbf N.
$$

Its three contributions are

$$
\begin{aligned}T_1&=(- v)(1) \\ &=- v.\end{aligned}
$$



$$
\begin{aligned}T_2&=(- 2 u - 2 v)(1) \\ &=- 2 u - 2 v.\end{aligned}
$$



$$
\begin{aligned}T_3&=(- u)(1) \\ &=- u.\end{aligned}
$$

Adding them gives the missing integrand:

$$
\begin{aligned}I(u,v)&=T_1+T_2+T_3 \\ &=- 3 u - 3 v.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore,

$$
\iint_S\mathbf F\cdot\mathrm d\mathbf S={\int }_{1}^{3}{\int }_{-2}^{4}I(u,v)\,\text{d}v\,\text{d}u.
$$

The missing expression is $- 3 u - 3 v$.

knowledge_point.title: Expressing Flux Over a Surface as a Repeated Integral

question.:question/problem:
Consider the vector field $\mathbf F(x,y,z)=⟨2 x,\,2 y - 2 z,\,2 x + 2 y⟩$ and the surface $S$ defined by $z=- 4 x + 3 y$ for $-1\le x\le 2$ and $-1\le y\le 3$. Orient $S$ so that its normal has a positive $\mathbf k$-component.

Using the parametrization $x=u$ and $y=v$, the flux through $S$ can be expressed as

$$
\iint_S\mathbf F\cdot\mathrm d\mathbf S={\int }_{-1}^{2}{\int }_{-1}^{3}\boxed{\phantom{AAAAAAA}}\,\text{d}v\,\text{d}u.
$$

What is the missing expression?
question.:question/worked-solution:
The parametrization and its parameter domain are

$$
\mathbf r(u,v)=⟨u,\,v,\,- 4 u + 3 v⟩
$$



$$
D=\{(u,v):-1\le u\le 2,\ -1\le v\le 3\}.
$$

Differentiate and compute the natural vector area element:

$$
\begin{aligned}\mathbf r_u&=⟨1,\,0,\,-4⟩ \\ \mathbf r_v&=⟨0,\,1,\,3⟩ \\ \mathbf r_u\times\mathbf r_v&=\begin{vmatrix}\mathbf i & \mathbf j & \mathbf k \\ 1 & 0 & -4 \\ 0 & 1 & 3\end{vmatrix} \\ &=⟨4,\,-3,\,1⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

The cross product already has the requested orientation, so

$$
\mathbf N=\mathbf r_u\times\mathbf r_v=⟨4,\,-3,\,1⟩.
$$

Write $\mathbf F=\langle P,Q,R\rangle$. Substitute all three coordinates into each component:

$$
\begin{aligned}P(\mathbf r(u,v))&=2 (u) \\ &=2 u.\end{aligned}
$$



$$
\begin{aligned}Q(\mathbf r(u,v))&=2 (v) - 2 (- 4 u + 3 v) \\ &=8 u - 4 v.\end{aligned}
$$



$$
\begin{aligned}R(\mathbf r(u,v))&=2 (u) + 2 (v) \\ &=2 u + 2 v.\end{aligned}
$$

Form the oriented dot product and collect like terms:

$$
I(u,v)=\mathbf F(\mathbf r(u,v))\cdot\mathbf N.
$$

Its three contributions are

$$
\begin{aligned}T_1&=(2 u)(4) \\ &=8 u.\end{aligned}
$$



$$
\begin{aligned}T_2&=(8 u - 4 v)(-3) \\ &=- 24 u + 12 v.\end{aligned}
$$



$$
\begin{aligned}T_3&=(2 u + 2 v)(1) \\ &=2 u + 2 v.\end{aligned}
$$

Adding them gives the missing integrand:

$$
\begin{aligned}I(u,v)&=T_1+T_2+T_3 \\ &=- 14 u + 14 v.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore,

$$
\iint_S\mathbf F\cdot\mathrm d\mathbf S={\int }_{-1}^{2}{\int }_{-1}^{3}I(u,v)\,\text{d}v\,\text{d}u.
$$

The missing expression is $- 14 u + 14 v$.
